statement: For a closed locally compact subgroup Q of the compact-open homeomorphism group of a connected noncompact second-countable surface without boundary, acting freely and properly, inclusion of its centralizer induces an injection on fundamental groups. Consequently every open orbit of a canonically lifted hyperbolic centralizer loop has an intrinsic based null-homotopy commuting with the full restricted operator stabilizer, including its restriction kernel.
depends_on: Pardon 2013 Theorem 1.5 and the stated Hilbert-Smith reduction, applied through the faithful product action on O times R; Palais 1961 Theorem 2.3.3, with the explicit free-action trivialization also verified in Kramer--Murat Garcia 2026 Theorem 3.7; invariance of domain and local surface homology; C.27 line median contraction; C.29 zero-winding circle contraction; C.30 proper closed operator image; C.32 discrete case and ambient-null restriction
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b) infinite-operator request; arbitrary proper-closure open-orbit reduction for C.12
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The action and topology used in the Lie and slice theorems are stated explicitly. The quotient is proved to be a one-manifold; the original operator group is not assumed discrete, effective on the orbit, or locally compact.
notes: The dimension-two case identifies the centralizer with right translations and makes evaluation a homeomorphism. The dimension-one case gives explicit A times B coordinates and proves that the discrete component quotient acts freely and properly on B. Its translation or finite-rotation generator is changed by explicit fibre coordinates to (a,b) maps to (lambda a,beta b), retaining lambda=-1 in finite even-component extensions. The centralizer is exactly the product of the functions phi with phi beta=lambda phi and the base homeomorphisms psi commuting with beta. Real scaling, based zero-winding circle lifts, and C.27/C.29 provide the contraction. This includes circle fibres with a Z action on a line base. This claim itself supplies intrinsic open-orbit contractions. C.34 subsequently proves continuity on the full nonopen locus, C.35 proves that its particular median prescription need not extend equivariantly, and C.36 gives compatible dimension-two closure contractions with continuity on finite unions. C37 supplies uniform three-word control and continuity on X2, the closed union of all dimension-two proper-image open orbits, including infinite accumulation. The remaining requirement is extension across X2 to its exterior, with frontier compatibility and accumulation control for the other proper operator cases, as recorded in C12.
